defs_parts: Four labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
Glossary only: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: Pan, tilt and roll turn the camera on the spot.
Dolly, truck and pedestal move the camera and keep it facing the same way.
An orbit circles the subject and keeps it framed, where a pan can lose it.
A zoom changes the lens, and a dolly moves the camera.
Parallax means near things shift more than far ones when the camera moves.
A deadzone waits, smoothing trails, look-ahead leads, and limits stop the view.
bookends.segment: Name The Camera Move, Defend It
bookends.command: Quiz me on camera terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use pan, tilt, truck, pedestal, dolly, zoom, orbit, parallax, deadzone and look-ahead. Describe what a camera does in a game or a cutscene, and I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case describes a camera in a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
